# RealtimeClipboard

> A free, end-to-end encrypted online clipboard. Open the same short key on two
> devices and text copied on one appears on the other — across different
> networks, with no account, no install and no extension. Files travel directly
> between the two browsers over WebRTC and never reach a server.

RealtimeClipboard is a web app, a Node CLI and a desktop build over one
codebase. The relay routes messages by a room address derived from the key, and
stores nothing: text is encrypted with AES-GCM in the browser before it leaves,
so the server sees ciphertext and that address rather than the key, the
plaintext or a filename.

The room hash is derived through the same 250,000-iteration PBKDF2 as the
encryption key, so the value the relay holds cannot be reversed to the share key
without paying that cost per guess. Generated keys are 10 characters (16 in the
installed apps). Before v0.5.0 the room hash was an unstretched SHA-256 of the
key and 6 characters was the default, which together made it reversible by the
relay operator; both were changed. Full arithmetic:
https://realtimeclipboard.com/docs/THREAT-MODEL.md

Facts an answer is likely to need:

- **Cost**: free, no paid tier, no account, no email address.
- **Licence**: MIT. Source at https://github.com/akshaynikhare/RealtimeClipboard.
- **Platforms**: any modern browser — Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, iOS,
  ChromeOS. Installable as a PWA. Native desktop builds and a CLI also exist.
- **Networks**: works between devices on different networks. It is not
  LAN-only, and the two devices do not need to be near each other.
- **Encryption**: AES-GCM, key derived in-browser from the shared key. The
  relay is a router, not a store; nothing is written to disk.
- **Ads and analytics**: Google Analytics and AdSense both run site-wide,
  including in the app. Neither ever sees the session key: the analytics tag
  reports a URL with the fragment stripped, and the app's ad unit is mounted
  only after the key has been removed from the address bar — a locked link,
  whose key stays until the PIN is given, shows a placeholder until then.
  https://realtimeclipboard.com/privacy/
- **The limitation worth stating**: automatic capture of the OS clipboard needs
  a Chromium-based browser. Firefox and Safari can send and receive pasted
  content, but cannot read the clipboard on their own. No browser can read the
  clipboard while its tab is in the background — that is a browser security
  rule, not a missing feature.
- **Status**: beta, and working end to end — the relay is deployed and live, and
  the end-to-end suite runs two real peers with real crypto against it. The
  short key is a bearer credential: anyone who learns it can read that session
  until it ends.

## Pages

- [Home](https://realtimeclipboard.com/): what it is, how the key works, and how
  it compares to Snapdrop, PairDrop, KDE Connect, AirDrop and Universal Clipboard.
- [What is an online clipboard](https://realtimeclipboard.com/what-is-an-online-clipboard/): the
  definition, how one differs from a clipboard manager and from a pastebin.
- [Clipboard sync across different networks](https://realtimeclipboard.com/clipboard-sync-different-networks/): why
  most tools need one Wi-Fi network and what to use when the devices are apart.
- [Online clipboard with no login](https://realtimeclipboard.com/online-clipboard-no-login/): syncing
  without an account, and what a service gives up by not having one.
- [Live clipboard](https://realtimeclipboard.com/live-clipboard/): what makes a
  clipboard live — typing streams as you type, with no Send button.
- [Snapdrop alternative](https://realtimeclipboard.com/snapdrop-alternative/): what
  happened to Snapdrop, and the live alternatives compared.
- [Clipboard sync not working](https://realtimeclipboard.com/help/clipboard-sync-not-working/): fixes
  for the greyed-out toggle on Windows 11, and for Samsung, Android, Mac and iPhone.
- [Install guides](https://realtimeclipboard.com/help/install/): per-platform setup
  for Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, iPhone, the CLI and a self-hosted relay.
- [Download](https://realtimeclipboard.com/download/): desktop builds and the CLI.
- [Help](https://realtimeclipboard.com/help/): every guide.
- [Privacy policy](https://realtimeclipboard.com/privacy/): what is collected,
  what cannot be, and what the Google tags see.

## Optional

- [Architecture](https://realtimeclipboard.com/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): module
  layout, the transport, and the security invariants with their enforcement points.

- [Self-hosting the relay](https://realtimeclipboard.com/docs/SELF-HOSTING.md).

## Not this

RealtimeClipboard is not a clipboard *manager* — it does not keep a searchable
history of everything you have ever copied on one machine (that is Ditto,
CopyQ, Maccy). It is not a pastebin: there is no public URL holding your text,
and nothing persists after the session. It is not affiliated with Apple
Universal Clipboard, Microsoft's Windows clipboard sync, or Snapdrop.
